notes: The last of the audit findings — the ones ranked lowest, two of which turned out not to be low at all. A RE-ISSUED CHEQUE no longer erases the month the original was outstanding in: re-issuing the same physical cheque after a reversal reuses its row and used to overwrite the issue date, which is the date the reconciliation reads — so a cheque written on 12 January, cancelled on 2 February and re-issued on 3 March stopped having ever been outstanding in January, and reprinting that already-signed-off month left the statement short by its value with no line to explain it. A BACKUP WITH NO CHECKSUM is no longer restored unverified: the archive used to be written into place before its checksum file, and a MISSING checksum was waved through while an empty one was refused; the checksum lands first now, and both the restore and the verify drill refuse what they cannot check. A DISMISSED COLLEAGUE can no longer send mail as the organisation — every screen and figure was already closed to them, but the actions that reach outside the books asked only whether somebody was signed in (signing in itself is unchanged: a new colleague still signs in and waits to be activated). ALSO: a funding petty-cash voucher printed 0.00 and “Zero Ghana Cedis” when its cheque entry was missing; withholding certificate numbers shifted when a sibling deduction was reversed, renumbering a certificate already in the withholdee’s hands; a drill-down quietly stopped excluding year-end closing entries on a failed lookup; the printed ledger’s columns totalled 109% of the page in the all-accounts view, so the narration column was silently narrower than intended; and a page-margin rule added for the ledger had moved EVERY printed document in the app from 16mm to 12mm and stripped the padding from the Official Receipt. Every fix is covered by a test checked against the defect itself.
